paper_title: ReGE: Stronger Agents through Experience Synthesis

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Repeated attempts at interactive tasks uncover facts, useful operations, and failures that can inform subsequent execution. We introduce ReGE, a framework for turning this recorded experience into guidance for a fresh attempt. Its main implementation, ReGE-Syn, uses a single coach call to jointly synthesize bounded execution records and available artifacts into self-contained guidance, connecting task-specific findings with proposed actions and relevant pitfalls. A student starts from the task's initial environment state and adapts this guidance to current observations. Source generation, synthesis, and student execution use the same base model, without parameter updates or a stronger teacher. Across four benchmarks, ReGE improves accuracy by an average of 9.9 percentage points for GPT and 8.8 percentage points for Claude compared with unguided execution. On matched BrowseComp-Plus subsets, ReGE-Syn reduces guidance-construction tokens by 98.2\% on GPT and 95.5\% on Claude relative to adapted AggAgent, with observed success. Combined construction and execution tokens decrease by 15.7\% and 35.4\%, respectively, counting input plus output and excluding source generation. BrowseComp-Plus ablations further associate access to process information with fewer student steps and show that joint synthesis produces substantially shorter guidance than Direct history or Independent summaries, with observed success. These results demonstrate how agents can use their own recorded experience to improve subsequent task completion, and suggest a low-cost way to consolidate the execution records of parallel agent systems such as agent swarms.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Repeated attempts can uncover solutions and information that single run misses (Brown et al., 2024; Snell et al., 2024). For interactive agents, these attempts produce more than candidate answers: they record discovered facts, useful tool operations, intermediate results, and failed strategies. This experience offers material for improving the same models subsequent actions. We ask: How can an agent turn experience from its own attempts into more effective subsequent execution? Useful discoveries can be distributed across attempts, while the complete records are long and the correctness of individual findings is unknown. Candidate selection, response aggregation, and trajectory summarization provide different ways to reuse prior attempts (Cobbe et al., 2021; Li et al., 2025; Kim et al., 2026). The challenge is to retain the details needed for subsequent actions while reducing the history new agent must process. file created or an application state Figure 1: With ReGE, gpt-5.6-luna matches gpt-5.6-sol at 28% of its cost. Costs include source pools; see Table 5.

sections.content: Figure 2: The joint-synthesis implementation of ReGE. The coach reads the rendered source pool; the student receives the resulting guidance and interacts with its own environment. Source generation, synthesis, and execution share the same base model. reached in previous attempt does not carry over when the environment is reset: the agent must perform the required operations against the current state. We introduce ReGE (Re-execution Guided by Experience), framework for constructing guidance from recorded attempts. Its main implementation, ReGE-Syn, presents bounded execution records and available artifacts together to coach, which produces self-contained guidance in one call. The coach connects task-specific findings with proposed operations and relevant pitfalls. fresh student starts from the tasks initial environment state, using current observations to follow, adjust, and verify the guidance. Source generation, synthesis, and student execution use the same base model, without parameter updates or stronger teacher; this lets us test whether lower-priced model guided by its own attempts can match higher-priced models. The framework also includes ReGE-Sel, which forwards one judge-selected trajectory as guidance (see 4.6). We evaluate ReGE on Terminal-Bench 2.0, Spider2-Lite, AndroidWorld, and BrowseComp-Plus with GPT and Claude model lines. Across four benchmarks, ReGE improves accuracy by an average of 9.9 percentage points for GPT and 8.8 percentage points for Claude compared with unguided execution. On subset, gpt-5.6-luna with ReGE reaches 67.4% average success, comparable to the 67.0% of the higher-priced gpt-5.6-sol, at 28% of its cost including source-pool generation (Figure 1). On matched BrowseComp-Plus subsets, ReGE-Syn reduces guidance-construction tokens by 98.2% on GPT and 95.5% on Claude relative to adapted AggAgent, with observed success. Although student execution uses more tokens, combined construction and execution usage falls by 15.7% and 35.4%, counting input plus output and excluding source generation. Further BrowseComp-Plus ablations examine which source information helps execution, how to organize multiple attempts, and how the guidances output form affects its use. Our contributions are: Joint synthesis of execution experience. ReGE-Syn connects concrete findings, operations, and failure lessons across recorded attempts into actionable guidance for fresh execution by the same base model. Capability gains with low guidance-construction cost. Across four benchmarks, ReGE improves mean task completion over unguided execution. On matched BrowseComp-Plus subsets, ReGE-Syn substantially reduces construction tokens relative to adapted iterative aggregation and retains lower combined usage after student execution. With ReGE, lower-priced model reaches the success of higher-priced model in its family at 28% of its cost.

sections.title: 2 REGE: EXPERIENCE-GUIDED AGENT EXECUTION
sections.content: ReGE is framework for constructing guidance from recorded experience and using it in fresh execution. Guidance can be built by jointly synthesizing multiple attempts (ReGE-Syn) or selecting one trajectory (ReGE-Sel). We focus on joint synthesis; 4.6 compares the variants. The student starts from the tasks initial environment state and uses the guidance alongside current observations.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Source generation, guidance construction, and student execution share the same base model, without parameter updates or stronger teacher. Figure 2 illustrates the synthesis implementation.

sections.title: 2.1 RECORDED EXPERIENCE
sections.content: A task consists of an instruction x, an initial environment state s0, and benchmark evaluator. Repeated attempts produce source pool = {τ1, . . . , τK}. For ReGE-Syn, we construct the text representation (P) programmatically: each attempt forms separate block, with available reasoning or action narratives and commands in step order, followed by final artifact paths and contents. These fields are copied and truncated to bound the input length; no per-trajectory LLM summary is generated before the coach sees them. Benchmark correctness labels are withheld from both coach and student. Raw per-step observation fields are omitted, so execution feedback is accessible only where preserved in the rendered text or artifacts. This representation provides bounded execution records rather than the complete environment history. Appendices A.1 and A.2 specify the field mappings, truncation limits, and prompts. 2.

sections.title: JOINT EXPERIENCE SYNTHESIS
sections.content: Useful experience can be distributed across attempts: one may uncover necessary task fact, another workable command, and another failure to avoid. ReGE-Syn brings these records into shared context and prompts coach to turn them into self-contained guidance for fresh attempt. Using the same base model with parameters θ, the coach Cθ constructs = Cθ(x, (P); psyn) , (1) where psyn specifies the guidance construction task. All retained source blocks are presented together, preserving attempt boundaries and step order. single coach call produces the guide, allowing decisions about what to retain and connect to account for information across attempts. Independent per-trajectory summarization makes these decisions separately before combining summaries. The coach is prompted to connect concrete findings with proposed operations and relevant pitfalls, retaining details needed to act on them. The default guidance is an execution-ordered plan. Exact paths, values, commands, format requirements, and encountered problems are placed alongside the steps where they matter. When the records support candidate answer or artifact, the coach is asked to include it together with way to verify it. The guide must be understandable without consulting the source attempts, since the student receives only the resulting guidance. Source correctness labels are unavailable, so its recommendations remain subject to the students checks against the current environment. ReGE-Syn shares joint aggregation with response-aggregation methods such as Self-MoA (Li et al., 2025). Here, the coach synthesizes bounded execution records and available artifacts into guidance for further interaction: the student must carry out and verify the proposed operations in fresh environment. Table 1 compares these design choices; 4.3 examines the value of process information, and 4.5 compares joint synthesis with alternative ways of presenting the recorded experience. sections.title: 3 EXPERIMENTAL SETUP
sections.content: Benchmarks. We evaluate on four benchmarks. Terminal-Bench 2.0 (The Terminal-Bench Team, 2025) includes 89 tasks, with budget of 30 agent turns per execution. Spider2-Lite (Lei et al., 2025) includes 135 instances with local SQLite databases; agents receive read-only access and up to 18 SQL calls. AndroidWorld (Rawles et al., 2025) uses the text-only T3A agent, with guidance supplied through its native task-guideline interface and step budget of ten times task complexity. After excluding two templates that crash the emulator, we evaluate 114 templates with three parameterisations on GPT and one on Claude, yielding 342 and 114 instances, respectively. BrowseCompPlus (Chen et al., 2025) includes 830 questions over fixed corpus of 100,195 documents. Agents use retrieval and document-opening tools without live web access, with 40-step budget. We use DeepSeek-V4-Flash with reasoning disabled as the LLM equivalence judge for BrowseComp-Plus. Models and budgets. We use gpt-5.6-luna and claude-sonnet-5, holding the base model fixed across source generation, guidance construction, and student execution. Source pools contain four attempts per task on all benchmarks (see Appendix B.1). ReGE and AggAgent share these pools and each receive one fresh student execution under the same benchmark-specific step limit to match the budget. Generation settings, effective serving limits, and collection exceptions are documented in Appendix A.3. Baselines. Control performs one unguided execution (pass@1) under the same student step limit. Our Reflexion adaptation (Shinn et al., 2023) allows up to three executions, using reflections from preceding trials and label-free self-evaluation for stopping. AggAgent (Lee et al., 2026) iteratively inspects source records using its released tools and prompts. To align it with our fresh-execution protocol, we adapt its final response into guidance for fresh student. Independent summaries, our agentic PDR adaptation (Kim et al., 2026), summarize four source trajectories separately and concatenate the summaries to guide fresh student (Appendix A.2). We also report two references without student re-execution: Self-Consistency (SC; Wang et al., 2023) votes over available source outputs, while Best-of-N reports the original score of the source selected by the judge model. Inference cost. Our primary cost metric is the sum of input and output tokens used after sourcepool generation, including all method-specific guidance construction and execution calls. Input-only usage and costs that include source generation are explicitly identified.

sections.title: 4 RESULTS
sections.content: Recorded experience strengthens execution by the same model. Across the four benchmarks, ReGE improves task completion over Control while keeping the base model fixed and requiring fresh student execution  (Table 2)  . For example, GPT success on Terminal-Bench 2.0 rises from 41.6% to 56.2%. Here, the student must use prior experience to perform the required operations in reset environment, so the gain reflects improved completion in new attempt. Joint synthesis provides low-cost way to construct such guidance: on matched settings, ReGE-Syn substantially reduces construction tokens relative to AggAgent while retaining lower combined construction and student-execution usage, excluding source generation.

sections.title: 4.1 EFFICIENT EXPERIENCE SYNTHESIS
sections.content: Joint synthesis makes effective guidance inexpensive to construct. On matched BrowseCompPlus queries, ReGE-Syn reduces construction tokens by more than 95% relative to AggAgent on both base models, while maintaining observed task success  (Table 3)  . Guidance construction consequently accounts for only small fraction of ReGE-Syns combined usage. These results show that consolidating prior attempts into useful guidance need not make construction the dominant inference expense. The construction savings translate into lower combined usage. Students guided by ReGE-Syn consume more tokens than those guided by AggAgent, partially offsetting the construction savings. However, the reduction in construction cost more than compensates for this additional student work. On these matched subsets, ReGE-Syn uses the fewest combined construction and execution tokens among Control, Reflexion, AggAgent, and ReGE-Syn. For Reflexion, construction includes selfevaluation and reflection, while execution sums token usage across all actor trials. This comparison counts input plus output tokens and excludes source generation. Experience guidance can reduce downstream execution effort. For claude-sonnet-5, ReGE-Syn uses fewer student output tokens and steps than unguided Control on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Spider2-Lite  (Table 4)  . On Spider2-Lite, SQL calls fall by 50% and output tokens by 30%, whereas both measures remain nearly unchanged on AndroidWorld. These results extend the efficiency analysis beyond BrowseComp-Plus and show that reductions in student effort vary across tasks.

We compare gpt-5.6-luna with ReGE against single unguided executions of two higherpriced models from the same family, gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol, and of the newer gpt-6-luna, which is priced below gpt-5.6-luna. Due to budget constraints, we use the first 50% of tasks by task ID on Terminal-Bench 2.0, Spider2-Lite, and AndroidWorld (task templates with one parameterization each on AndroidWorld) and the 300 BrowseComp-Plus queries used in our ablations. The other models use the prompts, tools, step limits, and graders of the main Control runs, and their results are paired by task with the gpt-5.6-luna results of Table 2, leaving 468 comparable tasks. On this subset, ReGE raises the average task success of gpt-5.6-luna from 56.8% to 67.4%, compared with 63.9% for gpt-5.6-terra, 67.0% for gpt-5.6-sol, and 49.4% for gpt-6-luna (Table 5 and Figure 1). Including source-pool generation, ReGE costs $0.21 per task at list prices, 58% of the cost of gpt-5.6-terra and 28% of that of gpt-5.6-sol; gpt-6-luna costs $0.009 per task. When the source pool already exists, ReGE costs $0.034 per task, 9% and 4% of the costs of gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol and close to the $0.041 of one unguided gpt-5.6-luna execution. sections.title: 4.3 WHAT INFORMATION MAKES EXPERIENCE USEFUL?
sections.content: Recorded experience makes coaching more effective. With claude-sonnet-5 on the same 300 BrowseComp-Plus queries, coaching without source experience performs to Control, while providing even one recorded attempt substantially improves success in Table 6. Increasing the source count from one to four adds another 4.0 percentage points. Source coverage and input length increase together, so this comparison does not establish gains at matched inference cost. Appendix B.1 provides the paired comparisons.

sections.title: 4.4 WHEN DOES RECORDED EXPERIENCE HELP?
sections.content: ReGE-Syn shows its largest gains on pools containing both successful and failed attempts. Table 8 compares ReGE-Syn with Control within source-quality groups. Mixed pools show the largest observed success-rate gains in all eight modelbenchmark combinations. Across TerminalBench 2.0, Spider2-Lite, and AndroidWorld, these gains range from 13.0 to 21.6 percentage points. On BrowseComp-Plus, they reach 48.0 points on GPT and 35.2 on Claude. These results show that source experience need not be uniformly successful to support more effective subsequent execution. Source quality also reveals the limits of experience reuse. Fresh successes remain possible when all source attempts fail, but improvements over Control are smaller and inconsistent. On GPT Terminal-Bench 2.0, success rises from 0.0% to 9.4%, whereas both methods remain at 0.0% on GPT Spider2-Lite. When all sources succeed, Control already solves at least 90% of tasks in every modelbenchmark combination, leaving less room for improvement. Appendix B.2 examines reexecution conditioned on successful selected source, and Appendix B.3 reports repeated-execution results. 4.

sections.title: 4.6 GUIDANCE VARIANTS
sections.content: Joint synthesis supports effective guidance beyond fixed execution plan. ReGE-A requests an explanation and answer while retaining ReGE-Syns coach, source pool, and delivery header. On the same 290 queries in Table 10, this change reduces combined construction and student-execution tokens by 32.1%, while observed success rises from 88.3% to 90.7%. Most of the savings come from student execution, with additional construction savings mainly from shorter coach output. The answer format does not lead in every tested setting: in separate comparison with gpt-5.6-luna on 100 BrowseComp-Plus queries with the same source pools and protocol, ReGE-A solves 80% of queries versus 82% for ReGE-Syn. Selecting one trajectory provides effective guidance. As shown in Table 10, ReGE-Sel achieves 89.3% success compared with 88.3% for ReGE-Syn, while using 21% fewer student tokens.

sections.title: 4.7 FROM RECORDED EXPERIENCE TO FRESH EXECUTION
sections.content: Concrete guidance supports verification and adaptation during execution. claude-sonnet-5 run on the Terminal-Bench 2.0 task db-wal-recovery illustrates how prior finding and failure lesson guide operations against the students current environment. Execution Case: Recovering Database from Its Log Recorded experience. Successful source attempts identify the XOR decoding key 0x42 for the databases write-ahead log. Another attempt opens main.db before making backup and loses main.db-wal, leaving the recovery incomplete. Synthesized guidance. The guide retains the decoding key and instructs the student to back up both files before opening the database, decode and check the log, and then recover the records. The case illustrates guidance that preserves concrete information and student that checks and adjusts the proposed operations. Student verification and adjustment. The student backs up its current files, verifies the key and decoded log, and moves the main.db-shm cleanup ahead of replacing the log and opening the database. The guide had suggested this cleanup only as fallback. The student exports 11 ordered records to recovered.json and passes all seven official tests. Incomplete attempts can still supply useful operational knowledge. In the AndroidWorld task BrowserMultiply, none of the four claude-sonnet-5 source attempts completes the task, but two reach working route for opening the local web page. Here the sources supply an access procedure rather than completed answer; the student must still obtain the page values and finish the interaction. Execution Case: Completing Browser Task from Unsuccessful Attempts Recorded experience. Repeated taps on task.html leave the file manager unchanged. Two attempts discover the route long-press More options Open with Chrome, but all four exhaust their 22-step budgets before completing the multiplication task. Synthesized guidance. The guide retains this opening sequence, warns against repeated single taps, and describes Chromes initial setup prompts. It asks the student to obtain the five numbers from the page and submit their product. Student verification and adjustment. The student uses the opening sequence immediately. When dismissing Chromes sync prompt returns it to the file manager, it repeats Open with Chrome to reach the page. It records the displayed numbers 9, 10, 9, 5, 5 during the five clicks and enters their product, 20,250. The page displays Success! and the benchmark records success after 19 steps, within the same 22-step budget as the sources.

sections.title: 5 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Aggregation of multiple attempts. Repeated sampling produces candidates that can be selected through voting (Wang et al., 2023) or evaluation (Cobbe et al., 2021), or combined through generative aggregation (Jiang et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024b). Self-MoA jointly aggregates responses sampled from single model (Li et al., 2025). AggAgent extends aggregation to long-horizon agentic tasks by using tools to inspect candidate solutions and retrieve information from their trajectories (Lee et al., 2026). ReGE-Syn shares the goal of combining useful information across attempts. It

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: jointly reads bounded execution records and available artifacts in one coach call, producing guidance that student uses during fresh interaction with the environment. Agent swarms decompose task into heterogeneous sub-problems that parallel sub-agents execute concurrently (Kimi Team, 2026); ReGE-Syn studies the complementary step of consolidating the records of parallel attempts at the same task into guidance for one fresh execution. Distillation for subsequent execution. Parallel-Distill-Refine constructs workspace for subsequent generations using operators that include joint global summarization and candidate selection (Madaan et al., 2025). Kim et al. (2026) adapt PDR to agentic coding by independently summarizing rollouts and concatenating selected summaries to condition new rollouts in freshly initialized environments. ReGE-Syn constructs guidance jointly from the retained source records, allowing content choices to account for information across attempts before producing the guide. Reflection and agent memory. Reflexion uses verbal reflections on task feedback to guide subsequent trials (Shinn et al., 2023). ExpeL extracts insights from accumulated experience (Zhao et al., 2024), while Agent Workflow Memory induces reusable workflows (Wang et al., 2024c). AutoGuide derives context-aware guidelines from offline experience (Fu et al., 2024), and AutoManual organizes knowledge acquired through interaction into instruction manuals (Chen et al., 2024). Voyager stores executable skills for later reuse (Wang et al., 2024a); A-MEM organizes experience into linked notes and revises existing memories as new information arrives (Xu et al., 2025). We study task-specific reuse, asking how records from multiple attempts at the same problem can support new execution with the same base model.

sections.title: 6 LIMITATIONS AND CONCLUSION
sections.content: Due to computational budget constraints, our evaluation is limited to four benchmarks: TerminalBench 2.0, Spider2-Lite, AndroidWorld, and BrowseComp-Plus, with ablation studies conducted on selected subsets of the evaluation data. Further evaluation should cover broader task settings and repeated executions with aligned settings. We presented ReGE, framework that turns recorded attempts into guidance for fresh agent execution. Its main implementation jointly synthesizes concrete findings, operations, and pitfalls in single coach call. Across four benchmarks, experience-guided execution improves mean task completion while keeping the base model fixed. On matched BrowseComp-Plus subsets, joint synthesis sharply reduces guidance-construction tokens relative to adapted iterative aggregation and lowers combined construction and execution usage, excluding source generation. BrowseComp-Plus analyses further support compact experience reuse through multiple guidance forms. These findings establish practical way to make an agents prior attempts useful for subsequent action.

sections.title: AI USE STATEMENT
sections.content: We used generative AI tools to assist with language polishing and textual revisions of the manuscript, including improvements to clarity, grammar, and presentation. The authors take responsibility for the final content of the paper.

sections.title: ETHICS STATEMENT
sections.content: The benchmarks used are public research benchmarks with no human subjects; AndroidWorld runs in an emulator and BrowseComp-Plus uses fixed offline corpus, so no real user accounts are accessed. The methods reuse an agents own attempts and do not require additional data collection. We see no direct potential for harm beyond that of stronger autonomous agents in general.

sections.title: A EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOLS
sections.content: A.1 SOURCE REPRESENTATION Fields and artifacts. Artifacts are produced files on Terminal-Bench 2.0, submitted SQL and query results on Spider2-Lite, submitted answers on BrowseComp-Plus, and action narratives and the final action summary on AndroidWorld. Empty or non-submitting attempts remain in the pool. Truncation and overflow. ReGE-Syn, ReGE-Sel and ReGE-A retain at most 120 rendered steps per source, with reasoning and commands truncated to 200 and 160 characters per step, respectively. Each artifact is capped at 6,000 characters. If the combined source serialization exceeds 350,000 characters, all artifact bodies are removed while their paths remain. Any remaining excess is truncated at that limit and followed by an explicit marker. Direct history uses step-only rendering that omits tool observations and separate final-artifact blocks. A.2 PROMPTS AND GUIDANCE DELIVERY The boxes reproduce construction prompts and delivery text, with placeholders and line breaks normalized for typesetting. ReGE-Syn: Joint Synthesis Prompt System message. You are an aggregation agent: several independent agents attempted task (correctness unknown) and you synthesize the single best guidance for fresh agent. You do NOT have access to the ground truth solution. User message. TASK: instruction independent previous attempts (full trajectories + final files): serialized source pool Write an EXECUTABLE STEP-BY-STEP PLAN for fresh agent that will solve the task from scratch: (1) numbered steps in execution order, each concrete enough to act on; (2) the critical facts the attempts uncovered exact paths, values, commands, formats, edge cases placed at the steps where they matter; (3) pitfalls the attempts exposed and how to avoid them. If the evidence already supports final answer or artifact, state it in the plan together with how to verify it. The plan must be self-contained: the fresh agent sees only this plan, never the attempts. ReGE-A: Alternative Construction Request Produce your solution as single string with exactly two XML sections: <explanation>...</explanation><answer>...</answer>. The explanation must be self-contained reader who never saw this prompt understands how the answer was derived. The answer is your best final solution to the task. ReGE-Sel: Trajectory Selection Prompt System message. You judge agent trajectories. User message. TASK: instruction independent agents attempted this task (success labels hidden): rendered source trajectories Which ONE rollout is most likely FULLY correct end-to-end? Reply with EXACTLY one rollout id (e.g. claude-sonnet 1) and nothing else. Up to eight judge attempts seek parsable rollout ID, with requested output limits given in Table 11. Parsing prefers an exact ID, then the last valid ID mentioned; if all attempts fail, it selects the first source without consulting correctness labels. Cached picks avoid repeating selection during student collection.

sections.title: Student Delivery Headers
sections.content: Coach outputs (ReGE-Syn, ReGE-A, and Closed-book). ## GUIDANCE (synthesized by an aggregation agent that inspected several previous independent attempts at this task; follow it but verify as you go): Selected trajectory. ## PREVIOUS AGENTS COMPLETE ATTEMPT (judged most likely correct among several independent attempts; follow it but verify as you go): (chosen: rollout ID, label-free judge) Guidance precedes the instruction on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Spider2-Lite, enters the native T3A task-guideline interface on AndroidWorld, and is appended to the user message on BrowseCompPlus. The experiments use same-model source pools. AndroidWorld: Reset and Verification Instructions GPT header and instruction. ## RESET-AND-VERIFICATION GUIDANCE The following material comes from previous attempt at this task. Your environment has been reset to its initial state. Use current observations to determine which actions are needed, and verify the current task state before declaring completion. Claude instruction, following the selected-trajectory header. The following record comes from separate, earlier execution. The environment for your current execution has been reset to the tasks initial state. Statements about actions taken or completion in the record describe that earlier execution only; they do not establish the state or completion of your current task. Independent-summary construction. Each independent-summary call receives the task and one block from ReGE-Syns bounded pool serialization, inheriting its truncation and artifact-redaction task requiredecisions. The reconstructed prompt requests one JSON object with four groups: ments, agent actions, artifact changes, and command execution. Initial length instructions allow approximately 1,000 words, six command entries, six items per list, and 250 characters per string, prioritizing concrete commands, paths, values, and failure causes. Up to three formatting attempts retain the first complete JSON object containing the required taskrequirement and agent-action keys. Retries request 500 words, three commands, four items per list, and 120 characters per string; the output-token request remains fixed at the value in Table 11. If none passes, the last nonempty response is kept and flagged; an all-empty response becomes placeholder. There is no quality-based selection or fallback to raw trajectories. Usage counts all recorded calls for each delivered summary, including its original generation when cached summary is reused. A.3 EVALUATION AND TOKEN ACCOUNTING Serving and collection conditions. sections.content: Task selection. Each AndroidWorld template uses its first parameterization, the one also used for claude-sonnet-5. On BrowseComp-Plus, the comparison uses the 300 queries of our ablations. The selection depends only on task order, not on any results. Execution. gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-6-luna each run once per task without guidance, with the prompts, tools, step limits, and graders of the main gpt-5.6-luna Control runs. sections.title: E ADDITIONAL EXECUTION CASES AND EVIDENCE
sections.content: The cases below use recorded claude-sonnet-5 executions and the same sourceguidancestudent structure as 4.7. E.1 EVIDENCE FOR THE MAIN-TEXT CASES Table 15 documents the starting conditions and record linkage for the two main-text cases. Table 15: Record checks for the main-text execution cases. Check Recorded evidence Database initial state Browser task instance Record linkage Initial database and log fingerprints match across the source attempts and student; source-created backups and recovered outputs are not inherited. Source and student task parameters, both random seeds, and the 22-step budget match. The collector resets and initializes each task. Saved summaries record the opening sequence, product entry, and success message. Student records lack an injected-guidance hash; linkage uses saved guides, construction/execution logs, and collector configurations. E.2 ADAPTING DATABASE QUERY TO STORED VALUES Spider2-Lite task local098 asks how many actors have no four-year interval without film credit between their first and last credited years. Execution Case: Checking Year Formats before Counting Actors Recorded experience. The four sources return different counts after varying how they parse Movie.year and bound the gaps between credited years. Some extract the last four characters; others cast or filter the raw year strings. Synthesized guidance. The guide retains distinct actoryear pairs and LAG calculation, with consecutive credited years at most four years apart. It also recommends filtering for raw four-digit year strings and asks the student to inspect the stored format first.

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Student verification and adjustment. The student queries nonstandard year strings and their four-character suffixes, then checks for nulls and invalid suffixes. Its final query uses CAST(substr(year,-4) AS INTEGER) instead of the guides strict raw-string filter, while retaining the proposed gap calculation. Execution outcome. The submitted query returns 28,699 actors, matching an accepted official result. The record contains ten SQL calls. The student retains the query structure while adapting preprocessing to the data. Intermediate calls retain SQL prefixes and status flags; the final query and result CSV are complete. E.3 REUSING DOCUMENT LEADS FOR FRESH VERIFICATION BrowseComp-Plus query bcp-285 asks for the student who succeeded scientist as director of research center, using clues about the center, the scientist, and co-edited publication. Execution Case: Following Research Lead through Source Documents Recorded experience. One attempt reaches the Citrus Experiment Station and Herbert J. Webber, then submits Leon Dexter Batchelor. Two other attempts reach relevant documents without submitting an answer; the remaining attempt spends its budget on other leads. Synthesized guidance. The guide retains the institution and person names, document IDs 9606 and 26507, and reminder to read beyond the first excerpt. It prioritizes this lead and lists clues that still require checking. Student verification and adjustment. The student searches for the institution, reads document 9606 at offsets 0 and 6,000, and opens Webbers biography in document 26507. These passages provide the succession and biographical evidence; an additional search checks the University of Nebraskas charter date. Execution outcome. The student submits Leon Dexter Batchelor, which receives an exact-match success grade, after six recorded tool steps including submission. The guide preserves both candidate answer and the document locations that let the student check the research lead.
